title: wger-india food entry
description: One food for `manage.py import_food_json`. All nutrition values are PER 100 g (or per 100 ml for drinks) of the food AS EATEN (cooked, unless the name says dry/raw). The importer accepts a single object or an array of these objects. Energy should satisfy the 4/4/9 rule (protein*4 + carbs*4 + fat*9) within ±15%; larger deviations are rejected unless --override-kcal-check is passed.

name.description: Display name. Convention: 'Food name (state)', e.g. 'Moong dal (cooked)', 'Soya chunks (dry)', 'Kaju katli'. State the cooked/dry/raw state explicitly whenever it is ambiguous.

carbs_g.description: Carbohydrates in g per 100 g (available carbohydrates, i.e. excluding fiber).

sugar_g.description: Optional: sugars in g per 100 g (subset of carbs_g).

sat_fat_g.description: Optional: saturated fat in g per 100 g (subset of fat_g).

fiber_g.description: Optional: dietary fiber in g per 100 g.

sodium_g.description: Optional: sodium in g per 100 g (salt / 2.5).

brand.description: Optional: brand name for packaged products, e.g. 'Nutrela'.

barcode.description: Optional: EAN/UPC barcode of the packaged product.

source_name.description: Optional: where the values come from, e.g. 'IFCT 2017', 'product label', 'estimate'. Defaults to 'wger-india json import'.

portions.description: Optional: human portion presets shown when logging, each mapping a named portion to grams. Common ones: katori = 150, roti = 45, glass = 250, handful = 30, piece = weight of one piece, tbsp = 15, tsp = 5.

grams.description: Weight of one such portion in grams (use ml ≈ g for drinks).
